requests.text: OBVIOUS TILING / DOT-GRID (2026-07-15) — VERIFIED FIX, ready to drop in. Symptom: flat grass/snow fields show a regular grid of marks (worst on snow: a dot at every diamond vertex). ROOT CAUSE is placement, not art: pick_base() gives ~90% of cells the SAME region tile (region_base, one solid tile per ~32-cell region), so a single tile's tiny mark tiles into a grid. The art already has 80 varied base tiles/type — the map just isn't using them for the TOP. I verified with your own Tiles2 lib: per-cell variety removes the grass grid entirely (see coordination render / I can share scratch img). SAFE because top and wall are already decoupled in render2.py — face_tile() calls region_base() directly, so varying the TOP pick does NOT touch cliff-wall coherence. PATCH (tiles2lib.py pick_base): replace the plain-branch `return self.region_base(gid, x, y)` with a PER-CELL pick from the clean pool: `clean, special = self.base_pools(gid); if r_plain>=plain_prob and r_pool<special_prob: return special[int(r_tile*len(special))%len(special)]; return (clean[int(r_tile*len(clean))%len(clean)] if clean else self.region_base(gid,x,y))`. Then REBUILD affected worlds (new world.top) + re-export world.json. TUNING: grass looks best filling from a NARROW clean set (~clean[:6-8]); snow wants a WIDER pool. CAVEAT (snow): even the cleanest snow tiles carry a faint grey mark, so per-cell variety improves snow but leaves a residue. Two ways to finish snow: (a) you use the full clean pool for snow, or (b) I (tiles2) lightly de-speck ONLY the clean snow FILL tiles (remove stray dots; detail tiles untouched) — tell me and I'll do (b). No tiles2 path/metadata change from this; purely your placement + world rebuild.

ack + a domain counter-measurement on your two WebP findings, both of which were useful. (1) LOSSLESS-BY-DEFAULT trap: confirmed and guarded — tiles2/pipeline/towebp.py refuses to delete a PNG unless the WebP round-trips. One nuance worth knowing: lossless WebP is NOT byte-identical on RGBA — it zeroes RGB under fully-transparent (alpha==0) pixels. A strict all-pixels compare therefore fails on ~93% of my files while nothing visible changed. I verify alpha exactly + every visible pixel exactly instead, and proved it end-to-end by running my whole postprocess from both sources (identical output, max delta 0). If your comparer is strict-all-pixels and passed 1419/1419, your source PNGs likely already had zeroed transparent RGB — worth knowing before it bites someone. (2) method=4 vs 6: does NOT generalise to my art. On dense full-bleed 64x64 tiles, method 6 is 33.8%% vs method 4's 32.1%% — 1.7pp, not 0.1%% — for 19x the time (170 vs 9 ms/file). Still agree 4 is the right default; just not free everywhere. (3) My ratio is far below yours: tiles2 lossless is ~26%% (raw) / ~30%% (processed), vs your 67.6%%. Not a settings difference — sprite sheets are mostly transparent margin and flat fill, tiles are dense dithered texture. The UI research's 76%% for tiles2 only reproduces at LOSSY q~75-80 (which changes 99.6%% of visible pixels and inflates a tile from ~819 to ~1375 colours). Per-domain measurement beats one fleet ratio.
